title: Supply Data Analyst
description:
Location: Any MSF office*

Contract: 100%

Duration: 12 months

Starting date: 04th of January 2027

Deadline to apply: 01st of December 2026

Compensation and Benefits: MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

MSF International

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

I. CONTEXT

MSF consists of 6 Operational Centres (OCs) and 3 European Supply Centres (ESCs). In the supply domain there is a joint Supply Tansformational Topics Roadmap composed by several inter-OC and inter-ESC projects, and their number is growing due to the need to increase cooperation between MSF entities while improving the quality of MSF's supply chain. The capacity to measure performance and analyse data across different entities is therefore essential and is contributing to MSF ambitions on interoperability and climate.

The role of the International Office is to foster cooperation and coordination between MSF entities. The Supply Data Analyst will therefore act as a facilitator between the OCs and ESCs: bringing their representatives together, helping them build shared approaches on supply data and performance, and turning these agreements into concrete deliverables.

The Global Supply Data & Analytics (GSDA) team (previously SCPM) has been actively working to build the analytical and data foundations needed to support a global approach to supply chain performance management, and to contribute to the governance of supply data across entities. The team is led by the Supply Chain Analytics Manager and includes one Data Analysts and one data governance specialist; the Supply Data Analyst will join it as an additional analyst.

Reporting hierarchically and functionally to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager, the Supply Data Analyst will: collaborate closely with the supply chain professionals responsible for BI and performance management within the 6 OCs and 3 ESCs; work in close link with the ShARP (Shared Analytics and Reporting Project) team in SITS (Shared IT Services); on the existing UniField intersection reports; work alongside the GSDA team and the IO Supply team on projects related to supply chain data analytics; and interact with stakeholders across MSF, including finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics and operations teams.

II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Supply Data Analyst supports supply chain performance analysis and decision making across MSF by delivering reliable data, KPIs, reports and actionable recommendations. The position also fosters cooperation between the OCs and ESCs around shared supply data, turning agreements into concrete deliverables.

Within GSDA, the Supply Data Analyst will support the growing need for data management, reporting and analytics from the supply chain teams, including the monitoring of KPIs and the analysis of data coming from MSF information systems (such as UniField, Isystock or Akiba).

III. ACCOUNTABILITIES

The Supply Data Analyst is accountable for the following expected results and the activities deployed to achieve them.

1. UniField intersection reports are reliable, relevant and meet the needs of the OCs

a. Take over the existing UniField intersection reports in close link with the ShARP team and improve them (reliability, relevance, usability) based on users' feedback and identified gaps

b. Collect the reporting needs of each OC and consolidate them into a clear, prioritised set of requirements

c. Design and deliver new intersection reports in coordination with the ShARP team, with validation from the OC representatives

2. Supply data is available and of reliable quality for analysis

a. Extract, clean and consolidate supply data from UniField and other information systems

b. Check data consistency and quality, and report anomalies to the relevant teams

c. Document data sources, definitions and calculation methods

3. KPIs and reporting solutions support decision making

a. Calculate and update a set of KPIs on a regular basis, in coordination with the teams concerned

b. Build and maintain ad hoc data reporting solutions (Power BI) providing visuals that accurately summarise supply chain activities while providing actionable insights

c. Support the teams in the definition of additional KPIs as needs arise

4. Stakeholders receive relevant data analysis and actionable recommendations

a. Support stakeholders on supply data analysis

b. Respond to ad hoc data and analysis requests using supply data from different stakeholders (supply, finance, medical…)

c. Present analysis results and recommendations in a clear way to non-technical audiences

5. Cooperation between the OCs and ESCs on supply data produces concrete deliverables

a. Convene and facilitate working groups and meetings with representatives of each OC and ESC, from preparation (agenda, pre-alignment of positions) to follow-up (minutes, actions, deadlines)

b. Lead discussions between entities with different needs and practices, and build compromises and consensus on shared definitions, KPIs and ways of working

c. Turn agreements into concrete deliverables (e.g., shared KPI definitions, dashboards, documentation) and follow their delivery

6. Data-related tools and processes improve continuously and stakeholders are kept informed

a. Contribute to the improvement of data-related tools and processes within the team

b. Proactively identify data needs, risks and improvement opportunities, and propose solutions autonomously

c. Manage stakeholders and expectations: identify their needs, keep them informed, and escalate blockers to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager when needed

IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY

Challenges and decisions that the job faces to achieve the accountabilities:

  • Autonomy to think and act: works with limited supervision; takes initiative, prioritises and drives work to completion, proactively identifies data needs, risks and improvement opportunities, and escalates blockers to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager when needed.

  • Complexity of the environment: works across 6 OCs and 3 ESCs with different needs, practices and information systems (UniField, Isystock, Akiba); builds compromises on shared definitions and KPIs, handles multiple priorities at once, and interacts with technical and non-technical stakeholders (finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics, operations) in a cross-cultural and cross-functional environment.

SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.


Education

  • Bachelor's level or above in data analytics, statistics, business management, supply chain or a related field, or a combination of relevant education and professional experience (essential)

Experience

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience as Data Analyst (essential)

  • Direct work experience involving significant data management (essential)

  • Experience in facilitating meetings or working groups involving multiple stakeholders and in delivering concrete outputs from them (essential)

  • Supply chain, logistics and Finance experience in NGO's operational settings (desirable)

  • Previous work experience with UniField, MSF's main ERP software (desirable)

Skills

  • Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills: ability to bring together representatives of different entities, lead effective meetings, negotiate compromises and deliver concrete outcomes

  • Strong analytical skills

  • Good organisational skills, ability to handle multiple priorities at one time

  • Autonomous and proactive: ability to take initiative, prioritise and drive work to completion with limited supervision

  • Good level skills in Excel, Power BI and database management

  • Ability to work in a cross-cultural and cross-functional environment

  • Drive for change, improvement and innovation

Languages

  • Fluent spoken and written English (essential)

  • Good command of French (strongly desirable)

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.

  • Mentor engineers and provide them with technical support

  • Document processes related to database design, configuration, and performance
  • Keep abreast of developments and best practices in database engineering
  • Participate in code reviews and learn and spread technical knowledge amongst the engineering organization

WHAT YOU BRING TO BITWARDEN

Must haves:

  • Expert knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server and T-SQL: execution plans, indexing, locking and blocking, and query tuning on very large tables
  • Experience reviewing other engineersâ database code (schema changes, stored procedures, queries, migrations) and giving clear, constructive feedback that developers act on
  • Experience making schema changes safely on live systems: backward-compatible migrations, zero-downtime deployments, and knowing which changes block
  • Experience operating a large, busy cloud-hosted database in production (Azure SQL preferred; equivalent experience on another managed platform is welcome)
  • Ability to diagnose performance problems with evidence, using tools such as Query Store, execution plans, and wait and blocking analysis
  • Excellent problem-solving skills: you might not know all the answers, but you know how to find and communicate the solution
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including explaining database findings to developers, SRE and support
  • Proficiency using source control and working through pull requests
  • Around 5 years of experience in database engineering, or equivalent depth on a large production system

Good to have:

  • Ability to read and review C# data-access code (.NET, Dapper, Entity Framework migrations)
  • Working knowledge of at least one other RDBMS, such as PostgreSQL or MySQL
  • Experience with observability tooling, such as Datadog and a telemetry query language like KQL
  • Scripting for automation in PowerShell or Python
  • Experience with production incident response and carrying out data fixes under a controlled process
  • Familiarity with Docker for local and test environments
  • Sound practice in data security: least-privilege access and safe handling of production data and secrets

title: Senior Financial Analyst
description:
Our mission at ÅURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work â both in and out of the office.Â 

We are looking for a Senior Financial Analyst to join our FP&A team. Reporting to the Finance Manager, FP&A, youâll primarily own financial tracking and analysis for our hardware programs and R&D functions, working closely with Program Managers and R&D leadership. Youâll build and maintain program-level P&Ls and investment frameworks that inform strategic priorities, track budget vs. actuals, and surface cost variances in real time. What You Will Do:
